result:
I fixed 10 of the 150 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings or the shared rules in the module docstring. After the fix, a script compared every rule against a version built straight from its docstring, using about 3,300 qty/unit combinations each (thresholds and points around them included). It also checked that negative inputs raise an error. All 150 rules now match.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | Used `round()`, against the rule that discounts round down to the won | `base * 15 // 100` |
| 14 | Cap only applied when the discount was over 200,000, so discounts between 100,000 and 200,000 weren't capped | Always apply `min(disc, 100000)` |
| 21 | Capped the price above the threshold before taking 3%, instead of capping the discount | Take 3% first, then `min(disc, 10000)` |
| 33 | Same conditional cap as 14 (only over 200,000) | Always apply `min(disc, 100000)` |
| 35 | Rate was 4%; docstring says 3% | 4 → 3 |
| 91 | Used `round()` | `base * 2 // 100` |
| 111 | Threshold was `qty > 20`, so exactly 20 units got no discount | `qty >= 20` |
| 115 | Rate was 16%; docstring says 15% | 16 → 15 |
| 137 | Rate was 9%; docstring says 8% | 9 → 8 |
| 138 | Used `round()` | Changed to `//` |

I left 13 more rules alone (08, 10, 18, 59, 72, 77, 87, 103, 105, 108, 120, 123, 141). They're written differently, using forms like `not qty < N`, `if disc > cap: disc = cap` and `100 <= qty`, but they give exactly the same results. In 72 and 123 the threshold check excludes the threshold itself, but these are marginal rules, so the discount at the threshold is 0 either way and the result doesn't change.

STATUS: DONE
